Letters to the Editor

Make Your Voice Heard in Print

Letters to the editor are one of the most effective civic actions available. Congressional staffers read local papers. Editors take notice when a topic generates multiple letters. And your neighbors — especially the ones who aren't on social media — read them too.

Published: Indivisible Tahoe Truckee in the Sierra Sun

This letter was published in the Sierra Sun as part of our chapter's Forest Service campaign. Read it, share it, and use it as a template for your own local paper.

Read the Letter →

How to Write Your Own

Keep it short

Most papers accept 200–300 words. Lead with your local connection — where you live, where you hike, what Forest Service land means to your community.

Be specific and personal

Name the specific ranger district, the trail, or the watershed that matters to your readers. Specific is more powerful than general.

End with a clear ask

Tell readers exactly what to do: call their representative, visit 5calls.org, attend your chapter event.

Key facts to include

  • ▸ The Forest Service has lost ~25% of its workforce since January 2025
  • ▸ The FY26 budget proposes a 65% cut to total Forest Service funding
  • ▸ 57 of 77 research stations are set to close
  • ▸ Wildfire prevention work dropped 35–44% in 2025
  • ▸ The FY27 markup is coming — this is our chance to stop it

Banner Actions

Show Up and Be Visible

Indivisible Tahoe Truckee has hosted banner actions — visible public demonstrations outside congressional offices, community events, and high-traffic locations. They're low-barrier (you just need bodies and a banner), highly visible, and great for local press.

What We've Done

Our chapter organized a banner event to raise visibility around the Forest Service cuts. We can share photos, logistics, and what we learned. If you're considering one in your area, reach out — we'll help you plan it.

Contact Us for Details →

Quick-Start Tips for a Banner Action

  • ▸ Pick a high-visibility location: congressional office, farmers market, trailhead, main street corner
  • ▸ Keep the message simple and readable from a distance: "SAVE THE FOREST SERVICE" / "FUND OUR PUBLIC LANDS"
  • ▸ Invite your local paper — a photographer showing up makes it count double
  • ▸ Have a QR code pointing to 5calls.org for passersby to take action on the spot
  • ▸ Even 6–8 people with matching signs creates a strong visual

Targeted Actions

Target the Decision-Makers

The House Interior Appropriations Subcommittee is where the FY27 budget gets decided. If your chapter is in one of these districts, you have extra leverage.

Subcommittee Members — Mixed or Skeptical on Cuts

These members have shown at least some concern about specific aspects of the restructuring. Constituent pressure from their districts matters most.

Mike Simpson (ID) Chair of the subcommittee. Backs HQ move but pushed back on wildfire consolidation: "Congress didn't go along with that." Constituent calls carry extra weight.
Mark Amodei (NV-2) Called workforce facts "not good" while tracking firings. Also led the public land sale amendment. A neighbor district — worth targeting.
Ryan Zinke (MT) Led the bipartisan fight to strip Forest Service land sales from the reconciliation bill. Called it a "red line." Co-founded the Public Lands Caucus. Can be pressured further.

Ideas for Actions at Congressional Offices

  • ▸ Candlelight vigil for lost Forest Service jobs
  • ▸ "Burying the Forest Service" — cover a uniform with dirt as a visual statement
  • ▸ Picket with lab coats: "Where Is Congress?"
  • ▸ Scientist and researcher testimonials on camera at the office steps
